name: Dark Fuchsia
lede: Dark Fuchsia is a dark, strongly saturated purplish red that our data files under the fuchsia flower, filed by Plochere's 1955 ISCC-NBS color dictionary and sitting almost on top of two other names in our library.

sections.title: A fuchsia word
sections.body:
Our naming data groups Dark Fuchsia with the plant-and-landscape words, tracing it to the fuchsia flower rather than to a pigment or a place [1]. The Plochere Color System filed this name in 1955 under ISCC-NBS block 237, "strong reddish purple"; by computed color distance, the hex itself reads closest to a different ISCC-NBS reference point, block 256's "deep purplish red," about 5 units away [1]. Wikipedia and the xkcd color survey of 2010 both carry the same name at the same hex, #9D0759 [1].

Two other names in our library sit close enough to count as near-duplicates: Deep Magenta, 0.8 units away, and Jazzberry Jam, 1.7 units away [2]. The nearest name that reads as a genuinely different color is [[berry]], 3.8 units off, which our computed comparison calls "almost the same" [3]. Measured in LCH terms, Dark Fuchsia sits at lightness 34, chroma 59 and hue 356 degrees: dark, strongly saturated, and just past red into purple [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a close match to Dark Fuchsia covers enough of the canvas in only 3, as photographed, which makes it rarer than 79 percent of the named colors we track [4]. In printed English the word peaked in the 2010s, though it rose fastest in the 1850s; because fuchsia is also a plant and not only a color word, that curve may track the flower as much as the shade [4].
